pairs.evidence: crates/apps/research/src/lib.rs:962 Research findings are keyed by their position in the model's output, so a reordered report re-keys every finding and makes up changed revisions. dedup-and-datasets names row position as a key that must never be used. hackernews also serializes rank, points and comments straight into the change hash (:341).

techniques.evidence: crates/apps/research/src/lib.rs:962 Index-based key. hackernews keys by HN id (good) but hashes the whole story, including positional rank and volatile counts, with no declared compared-field set.

crates/apps/hackernews/src/lib.rs:387 Extraction is written as per-site code with inline selectors rather than as a RuleSet with declared failure semantics. The repo has a rule DSL, but this app does not use it.
crates/apps/watch/src/lib.rs:246 watch preview: a live fetch (cache bypassed), the same production judge, no writes, and a writes receipt

crates/apps/watch/src/lib.rs:194 An empty extraction fails the job instead of reporting zero-change success. hackernews :323 does the same. Both lump drift and soft blocks into one error and do not classify which it was.
crates/apps/research/src/lib.rs:3 The model runs as an agentic synthesizer over heterogeneous sources, which the technique allows. No rule authoring happens here.
